image_description: A close-up, side-profile photograph of an iguana's head and upper neck. The image focuses on the texture of the scales, the eye, the subtympanic shield, and the jawline. The background is dark and out of focus.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop of the head; the full triangular shape and the extent of the dewlap are not fully visible or are cut off by the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The distinctive large, circular white scale (subtympanic shield) is prominently visible behind the jaw angle.
Only the head and neck are visible; the body is outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal crest is located on the back/neck midline, which is largely obscured or out of frame in this side-profile headshot.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the transition from smaller granular scales on the neck to larger, plate-like scales on the snout and cheek.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are not visible in this head-only crop.
